analysis_notes.summary: Torah #123 has zero bechina edges in the dataset. The source text is entirely practical advice about mikveh immersion and its health benefits (opening sweat pores), plus a note that religious self-mortification (סגופים) does not cause harm unless motivated by pride (גדלות). The teaching contains no bechina-type language — no 'X is an aspect of Y' identifications. All relationships are causal/practical (eitza): immersion opens pores, cold water blocks pores, pride causes harm from self-mortification. There are no conceptual identity statements to extract as bechina edges. This is one of the short practical sayings in Likutay Moharan Tinyana that does not employ the Rebbe's typical conceptual-equivalence framework.
